purpose: Audit the clickable mock for usability + consistency, then keep improving it in bounded tasks: make controls consistent, make interactions legible (drag/choose/create/save/modify), and deeply flesh out real video + image editing workflows.

loop.contextBudget: Each task must fit in ~200k context. The coordinator dispatches ONE task at a time to a fresh subagent (its own 200k), or resets its own context via /reset-context with the continuation 'go'.
protocol: On 'go': read this file. Pick the highest-priority task with status 'pending' whose deps are all 'done'.
Set it 'in_progress'. Dispatch to a subagent following shared/AGENTS.md (page authors) or, for shared-DS tasks, allow editing shared/photonz-ds.css + AGENTS.md.
Verify: curl the touched pages return 200, spot-check the specific fix, confirm consistency + copy rules (glass look, 4pt spacing, canonical controls, no em dashes, say 'agent' not 'Claude').
Mark 'done' with a short note. Append any NEW problems found to 'discovered' as new pending tasks.
If coordinator context is getting large, run /reset-context with 'go' so the next task starts fresh. State here is the single source of truth.

conventions.controls: ONE canonical control system (see task ctrl-system). Buttons: sizes sm/md/lg, variants primary/secondary/ghost/danger, plus icon-button; every control has visible hover/active/focus/disabled response. No ad-hoc square/tiny/round buttons.
conventions.look: macOS Liquid Glass: translucent materials, luminous edges, capsule controls, continuous rounding (see LIQUID GLASS pass in photonz-ds.css).
conventions.legibility: Every asserted interaction must be SHOWN, not just claimed: how to pick/drag a component, how a keyframe maps to a value over time, how a tool changes the canvas. Prefer real, resettable interactive demos over static pixels.
conventions.copy: Plain human language, no em dashes, never say 'Claude' (say 'agent').

tasks.title: VISUAL RULE 8 (shared DS): Library tiles must stay recognizable - justify/size the .libgrid so a card reads as a card (min tile width + auto-fill), never squeezed into skinny unrecognizable slivers
tasks.notes: DONE for tile SHAPE (the rule as written); tile HEIGHT budget is an open design call, see discovered/library-vertical-budget-fork. .libgrid was repeat(3,1fr) - a FIXED column count, so a 268px dock gave 76px tiles with a 46px thumb. Now repeat(auto-fill,minmax(96px,1fr)) so the DOCK decides the count (2 at rest, 4 widened), and .libtile .th is aspect-ratio:16/10 instead of a fixed 46px strip. auto-fill deliberately, NOT auto-fit: with 2 tiles in a wide container auto-fit would stretch each to half the width; auto-fill keeps them card-sized and leaves the empty tracks. Also raised .dgrp.grow floor 124->212 and its body 88->168 (strictly better, but does not fully solve the cut-off row - the chrome eats it). VERIFIED across 64 pages / 209 visible tiles: smallest tile 107px (was 76), 0 ellipsised names, 0 overflow. HEIGHT RESOLVED after the user chose option A (drop the body Import button): removed from 39 pages where the group HEADER already carries a + Import menu, so no affordance was lost. That cut the Library chrome 102px -> 77px, and the .grow floor moved 124/88 -> 244/200, so a WHOLE card row is now fully visible with the next row peeking as scroll affordance (verified whole=2 cut=0 on app-shell, editor, image, video, dsys, paint, states, typography). SIDE FIX along the way: --segmin was measured with scrollWidth, which returns max(content, clientWidth) and so reported the chip's CURRENT box once it was wider than its text - a feedback loop that grew the floor until a 4-chip scope wrapped. Now measured with width:max-content, which cannot drift.

tasks.title: VISUAL RULE 10 (shared DS): walkthrough nav. USER RESTATED THIS ANGRILY - it is still broken. (1) CONSOLIDATE the controls INTO THE BOX ABOVE THEM - the nav must live inside the step card, not as a detached bar underneath it. (2) Buttons RIGHT-ALIGNED, in the order RESET / BACK / NEXT. Never Back on one side and Next on the other. (3) ARROW-KEY navigation must work (left/right steps).
tasks.notes:
DONE, all three parts, shared DS only - zero page edits across the 12 walkthrough pages.
(1) CONSOLIDATED: the .wbar was authored as a SIBLING of .wt-steps, which is why it read as a detached strip under the caption card. ds.js now wraps .wt-steps + .wbar in a generated .wt-panel, the border/radius/background moved from .wt-cap up to .wt-panel, and the bar carries a border-top divider - so the caption and the controls are literally one box.
(2) ORDER: deleted `.wbar .wt-reset{margin-left:auto}` (that was what stranded Back at the far left and Next at the far right). ds.js reorders the bar's children IN THE DOM - dots, label, Reset, Back, Next - rather than with CSS `order`, which would have moved them visually while leaving tab order lying. .wlabel takes margin-right:auto so the trio sits together at the right edge.
(3) ARROW KEYS: keydown bound per .wt. A page with exactly one .wt responds without needing focus; more than one requires focus, since guessing would steal arrows from the wrong widget. Never intercepts arrows aimed at input/textarea/select/contenteditable, or any modifier combo.
VERIFIED in-browser on ALL 12 pages (walk, capture-wt, vector-wt, agent-generate-wt, video-animate-wt, img-grade-wt, component-configure-wt, img-retouch-wt, ds-build-wt, video-create-wt, composites, ui-build-screen): DOM order Reset<Back<Next, x-order 900<990<1077, trio adjacent and flush to the bar's right edge, bar AND caption both inside .wt-panel's box, ArrowRight advances a step and ArrowLeft goes back. 0 horizontal overflow. FOLLOW-UP (user, mid-vr6): the nav bar moved to the TOP of .wt-panel, above the caption. ds.js appends bar-then-steps and the divider is border-bottom. Rationale: the controls are what you drive the walkthrough with, so they must hold one fixed position instead of sliding down the page whenever a step's caption runs longer; bar-first also makes them the panel's first tab stops. Verified on all 11 walkthrough pages: DOM bar-first, bar above steps, flush (barBottom==stepsTop), order dots>label>Reset>Back>Next.

discovered.note: Zoom now changes grid density but the artwork stays the same size, so the readout can say 260% while 'Hero card 420x260' renders at 420x260. Honest fix: scale the canvas's centred artwork (.canvas>.selwrap) by --zoom and COUNTER-scale the selection chrome (.sel-ring border+inset, .handle size+offsets, .mtag) by 1/--zoom so rings and handles stay constant-size like a real editor. At zoom 1 it is a no-op, so default rendering cannot regress. NEEDS A CALL: it changes what zoom means across every editor page.

discovered.title: VR6 leftovers: 3 primitives that ARE duplicated across pages but whose bodies genuinely diverge, so they need a variable-driven DS version rather than a straight copy
discovered.notes: Found by the same duplicate-rule scan that drove vr6 (re-run it: the scan is 40 lines of python over each page's <style> block, grouping rules by normalised selector+body). (1) `.rng` slider + `::-webkit-slider-thumb`/`::-moz-range-thumb` -- 6 pages, 18 distinct rules; the base and both thumbs are identical, only focus/disabled states drift, so promote the base and the thumbs. (2) `.rrow` -- 6 pages, 15 distinct rules; the divergence is ONLY the first/last column widths (62/40, 64/42, 60/42), so promote it with `--rl-w`/`--rv-w` custom properties and let pages retune those. (3) the video timeline `.tlbar`/`.tlgrid`/`.tlz` -- 6 pages, 38 distinct rules for .tlgrid alone; this is a real component with real per-page extension, so it needs a designed DS version, not a lift. Also: `.apiline` (8 pages, 17 rules) and the lang-* specimen doc-block cluster `.blk/.bname/.bnum/.api/.intro/.dd` (6-7 pages) -- the latter is ds-specimen-card, and note `.dd` COLLIDES with a colour-dot class on one page, so that one needs a markup rename, not just a CSS move.
discovered.triage: Folded into the shared-DS cleanup queue task. Slider and timeline are now shared components; the remaining work is migrating the 6 pages that still hand-roll .rng and verifying the timeline adopters.

currentGoal: MODEL-DRIVEN REFINE LOOP (user-approved). The site is pretty but not cohesively designed. Establish the product MODEL first, then refine everything against it in a loop with clear success criteria. Canonical model = shared/PRODUCT-MODEL.md: ONE document engine; Image/UI/Video are workspaces (lenses) over the same layer stack; adjustment/filter layers apply to UI frames exactly as photos; Video = same doc + time; Tokens->Styles->Components->Design Systems with semantic binding (extract-from-URL, catalog, AI re-theme); everything is one command (UI==API==agent). 6 success criteria (one model written down; shell coherence; legible blank-slate entries; ONE walkthrough template; foundation-gated features; the build test). 3-zone IA: App Design (canonical) / Usage clickthroughs (folded per surface, one template) / Prototypes & Ideas (speculative). User wants to return to LOTS of improvements ready.
resume: ON GO: (1) server: cd docs/design/mocks; curl -s localhost:8791 >/dev/null || nohup node dev-server.mjs >/tmp/photonz-mock-server.log 2>&1 & disown. (2) NEXT TASK is `vr6-tier2-primitives` (in discovered) - .rng, .rrow (promote with --rl-w/--rv-w custom props, do NOT lift one page's column widths) and the video timeline. Then the older backlog: ds-consolidated-cleanup, supersede-workspace-switcher, ds-specimen-card, reaudit. (3) HOW TO FIND WORK: do not read 64 pages. Scan. Parse each page's <style>, group rules by normalised selector+body, rank by page count; anything identical across 4+ pages belongs in the shared DS. vr6-strip.py does the deletion half and is also a standing guard - it must always report 0 rules to remove. (4) VERIFY EVERYTHING in the browser, three ways, never by looking at it: (a) geometry diff of every element on all 64 pages before/after at 2px tolerance (below that, getBoundingClientRect rounding flips +/-1px and reports 50 false pages); (b) getComputedStyle assertions that the shared rule is IN EFFECT on pages that no longer declare it - presence in the file proves nothing, a stray */ once silently deleted a rule and every page still looked fine; (c) the standing sweep in shared/audit-sweep.js. All three run from ONE chrome-devtools evaluate_script call using hidden iframes. Stash the baseline in localStorage, NOT on window: evaluate_script runs in an isolated world and window does not persist between calls. STATE OF PLAY: vr1-vr6 done. 64/64 pages serve 200, sweep clean, zero issues. RESET CONTEXT between VR tasks.
